There's one particular image of my parent that haunts me still and I haven't really talked about it, but I think it's the moment they finally realised it was the end for them. They'd had a serious illness and it had spread, and they'd all of a sudden gone downhill pretty quickly, to the point where they weren't making sense and stuff and didn't really understand what was going on. They got taken into hospital because of an infection, and they're laying there in the hospital bed, their eye sight had started to go too because of the pressure in their head, and they're talking to me. "When I get out of here we need to go and see the optician because my eyes are bad" - they didn't say it as eloquently as that, their speech is slurred and they're struggling to find the right words. All of a sudden they turn to look at me and grab my hand, and they just stare at me for a good 30 seconds and squeeze my hand tighter. It's in that moment I feel like everything came into place in their head and they could think properly and they just understood that they weren't getting out of hospital again. So yeah, having to sit through things like this, you're honestly sometimes not sure whether or not your loved one would have just been knocked over one day. There's no right way to have someone die who is a part of your life and I don't know which i'd have preferred.
